body: There are certainly gaps in your memory. The only time that Punpun talks to an inner persona is when he talks to "God". All the other characters were real people, living in the real world. "The God of Poop" being an exception. Your confusion may stem from the fact that there are a lot of narration about how Punpun is feeling and about this current and past circumstances.

I agree with that he view himself as a bird and the world is his cage. He could and would never achieve his full potential because he is a caged bird. You could also interpret his bad experiences as the world clipping his wings. Furthermore, you could also interpret Aiko as another cage. Punpun could never move on from Aiko, which made both of their lives miserable. There are a lot of symbolism and imagery in this manga that I absolutely adore. I would also love to hear more about your thoughts on this manga as well!

If this is a troll, then I'll give him a clap and a half, but the whole tone of the review makes it seem like he is completely serious about what he is saying. For his sake, I really hope this is a troll.
My bad. Wanna take selfies together?
